Task 6 input, not testable on this platform: a column of numpy long doubles. On Linux x86-64 np.longdouble is 80-bit (itemsize 16), and Schema.from_data takes such a column (wire/dtypes.py:231-232 types any float over 4 bytes float64), so this is reachable there; on macOS arm64, where this phase ran, np.longdouble is float64. request_fixture_exclusions.messages-client/client.run/fitting-on-a-: SDMClient.for_databricks_serving makes a client whose transport says it serves no sessions; that capability check (transport.serves_sessions) stays in the Python wrapper's transport, which the core never sees.
request_fixture_exclusions.messages-request/client.run/predict-over: Builds a DuckDB database for the case and reads it with Schema.from_source. The Rust runner's DuckDB database answers only its catalog (what lists the tables, and the error of a table it lacks), and describing a table in its source reads its rows, so the runner cannot build this schema. The refusal of rows given as predict= is raised in PredictiveQuery.materialize (sdm_client/query.py), before anything is read; the core's copy of it is held to today's class, code and message through scripts/parity/request_host.py over a real DuckDB database by tests/rust_core/test_request_over_a_source.py.
